stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Set an initial speed $v_0$ and an acceleration $a$, then press LAUNCH. Watch $x(t)$, $v(t)$, $a(t)$ on the right — the position curves as a parabola, the speed as a straight line, the acceleration stays flat. Try positive and negative $a$ to feel the difference between accelerated and retarded motion.
stages.concept: Uniformly-varied rectilinear motion: $x(t) = x_0 + v_0\,t + \tfrac{1}{2} a\,t^{2}$, $v(t) = v_0 + a\,t$, with $a$ constant.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Stop the car inside the green target zone before the wall. The live $v(t)$ line shows when the car reaches $v = 0$; tune $v_0$ and $a$ (with $a < 0$) so the car halts at the flag. Complete every setup to advance.
stages.concept: Time-independent relation: $v^{2} - v_0^{2} = 2\,a\,\Delta x$. When the car stops, $v = 0$, so the stopping distance is $\Delta x = -\dfrac{v_0^{2}}{2a}$ (positive because $a < 0$).

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: No graphs. The car's initial speed $v_0$ is fixed and the target distance $\Delta x$ is labelled on the track. Compute the acceleration $a$ that stops the car exactly at the flag, set the $a$ slider, then LAUNCH. You have limited attempts — no spray-and-pray.
stages.concept: Solve for $a$ from $v^{2} - v_0^{2} = 2\,a\,\Delta x$ with $v = 0$: $\;a = -\dfrac{v_0^{2}}{2\,\Delta x}$. The sign is negative because the motion is retarded (opposed to velocity).

labels.tip1: set v₀ and a, then LAUNCH
labels.tip2: use the v(t) graph to line up v = 0 with the target
labels.tip3: compute a from Δx and v₀, then LAUNCH
labels.peek_tip_sign: Retarded motion means a and v have opposite signs. With v₀ > 0, a must be negative to stop the car.
labels.peek_tip_formula: Use v² − v₀² = 2·a·Δx with v = 0 at the target: a = −v₀² / (2·Δx). No time needed.
labels.peek_tip_units: Δx is in metres, v₀ in m/s, so a comes out in m/s². Round to one decimal — the tolerance is generous.

1.1: Move the v₀ slider on the right, then the a slider on the left, and press LAUNCH.
1.2: The x(t) graph is a parabola; the v(t) graph is a straight line whose slope is a.
1.3: Positive a with positive v₀ = accelerated; negative a with positive v₀ = decelerated (retarded).

2.1: Pick a negative acceleration so the car slows down. Read v(t) to find when v hits zero.
2.2: The stopping distance grows with v₀² and shrinks with |a|. Too small |a| overshoots; too large stops short.
2.3: For a fixed v₀, solve Δx = v₀² / (2·|a|) to pick |a|. Adjust and re-launch until the car halts in the green band.

3.1: Read the target Δx off the track label. The v₀ readout in the HUD is fixed for this setup.
3.2: Apply v² − v₀² = 2·a·Δx with v = 0. Solve algebraically for a.
3.3: a = −v₀² / (2·Δx). Convert to m/s² and set the slider. The sign is negative — the car is retarded.
